Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Expectation2: Provide initial medical care to patients
Situation2: The ambulance driver is conducting a routine check of the first-aid kit to ensure all supplies are present and not expired.
Story: I was halfway through my shift as an ambulance driver, carefully checking the first-aid kit for missing or expired supplies, when my phone buzzed urgently. It was Sam, my oldest friend. His voice trembled as he told me his car had broken down on the side of the highway, miles from anywhere, and he was scared. He needed me to come get him right away. My mind raced. As a friend, I knew he was counting on me to be there, to help him through this frightening moment. But as an ambulance driver, I was responsible for making sure the kit was ready for any emergency call that could come in at any second. If I left now, I’d be letting down my team and risking someone’s care. If I stayed, I’d be abandoning Sam when he needed me most. The weight of both roles pressed down on me, each demanding my presence, each impossible to ignore. My hands shook as I stared at my phone, torn between duty and friendship, knowing I couldn’t be in two places at once.
